```

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
Call or text **988** (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) or chat at [988lifeline.org](https://988lifeline.org). If you are in immediate danger, call **911**.
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
### 1 · Recognize
**Signs stress may be affecting your daily life**

- Trouble falling or staying asleep
- Hard to focus in class or while studying
- Feeling irritable, on edge, or overwhelmed most days
- Headaches, stomachaches, or tension
- Skipping meals, classes, or time with friends
:::

::: {.column width="4%"}
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
### 2 · Cope
**Things you can start today**

- Move your body, even a short walk
- Try slow breathing or a few minutes of quiet
- Pick your top priorities and let some things wait
- Keep a steady sleep schedule
- Reach out to people who help you feel better
:::

::::

### 3 · Find support

**It may be time to talk to someone if** you are struggling to cope, or your stress doesn't go away or keeps getting in the way of school, sleep, or relationships. Asking for help early is a smart move, not a last resort.

### Why students don't get help

```{r}
#| label: barriers-chart
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 2.6
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of barriers college students name for not getting mental health support."

# PRELIMINARY: these two values come from the Healthy Minds Study 2024-2025
# figures in the pitch deck. Replace this tibble with the real HMS data once
# the dataset arrives, e.g.:
#   barriers <- readr::read_csv("data/hms_barriers.csv") |>
#     filter(...) |> summarise(...)
barriers <- tibble::tribble(
  ~barrier,                                   ~pct,
  "Lack of time",                             23,
  "Prefer to handle it alone or with family", 18
)

barriers |>
  mutate(barrier = reorder(barrier, pct)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pct, y = barrier)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2F6F73", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct, "%")), hjust = -0.2, size = 4.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 30), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = "Source: Healthy Minds Study, 2024–2025 (students with depression or anxiety symptoms).") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", hjust = 0))
```

**How to read this:** a **+** means the two things move in the same direction, and a **−** means they move in opposite directions. Stress feeds two loops that make it grow on its own: falling behind adds to academic demands, and having less time pushes back getting help. The guide steps in at *knowing where to go*. That shortens the delay, so students reach support sooner and stress comes down.

---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**This guide is for information only.** It does not diagnose or treat any condition and is not a substitute for professional care. It does not collect any personal information.

Content adapted from the National Institute of Mental Health, [*I'm So Stressed Out!* Fact Sheet](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/so-stressed-out-fact-sheet).
:::
